author_or_org: Qiming Zeng, Hao Luo, Yuhao Lin, Yicheng Jin, Yuxiang Wang, Fangcheng Fu, Xiao Yan, Jiawei Jiang

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: GraphRAG enhances LLMs to generate quality answers by retrieving contexts from knowledge graphs.
claims.quote: By retrieving contexts from knowledge graphs, graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) to generate quality answers for user questions.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The current answer evaluation framework for GraphRAG has two critical flaws: unrelated questions and evaluation biases, which can produce biased or wrong performance conclusions.
claims.quote: However, we observe that the current answer evaluation framework for GraphRAG has two critical flaws, i.e., unrelated questions and evaluation biases, which may lead to biased or even wrong conclusions on performance.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The paper proposes an unbiased evaluation framework using graph-text-grounded question generation to produce questions more related to the underlying dataset and an unbiased evaluation procedure to eliminate biases in LLM-based answer assessment.
claims.quote: To tackle the two flaws, we propose an unbiased evaluation framework that uses graph-text-grounded question generation to produce questions that are more related to the underlying dataset and an unbiased evaluation procedure to eliminate the biases in LLM-based answer assessment.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Applying the unbiased framework to 3 representative GraphRAG methods shows performance gains much more moderate than previously reported.
claims.quote: We apply our unbiased framework to evaluate 3 representative GraphRAG methods and find that their performance gains are much more moderate than reported previously.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The authors state their evaluation framework may still have flaws but argue that scientific evaluations are needed to lay solid foundations for GraphRAG research.
claims.quote: Although our evaluation framework may still have flaws, it calls for scientific evaluations to lay solid foundations for GraphRAG research.
